CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS OF GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important role in the development of a nation. Women as mothers of the nation who will give birth to children and children as the next generation of the nation are the capital of national development that need to receive legal protection from acts of gender-based violence and against children.

Gender-based violence and violence against children are increasingly prevalent today. Several forms of violence against women and children occurring in society may include social harassment, rape, trafficking of women and children, pornography, sexual exploitation, neglect, domestic violence. Therefore, legal instruments are needed that can guarantee the implementation of protection for the rights of women and children both at the national and regional levels.

In order to realize protection of the rights of women and children from the threat of acts of violence as mentioned above, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Central Government hereinafter referred to as Government is the President of the Republic of Indonesia who holds the governmental power of the State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
2. Region is Kudus Regency.
3. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
4. Regent is the Regent of Kudus.
5. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter referred to as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Kudus Regency.
6. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit responsible for women's empowerment and child protection.
7. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
8. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society.
9. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
10. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
11. Protection implementation is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the responsible SKPD.
12. Violence is any form of unlawful act that can result in or cause harm to a person whether physical, sexual, psychological and economic in nature.
13. Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment carried out on the basis of gender and aimed at reducing, eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
14. Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment carried out against children, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.
15. Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, illness, or serious injury.
16. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
17. Psychological Violence or psychic violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person.
18. Economic Violence is any act that may include restricting a person's right to work properly inside or outside the home and also acts of neglecting family members in the form of not providing proper livelihood, care or maintenance.
19. Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who because of their gender experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses caused by state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
20. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment whether physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual, and other losses caused by state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
21. Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to become more empowered, whether physical, psychological, social, economic or sexual.
22. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems they face.
23. Integrated Services is a series of activities to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unified implementation, prevention efforts, health services, medicolegal services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
24. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes that can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.
25. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with established operational standards.
26. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations, and/or community organizations.

CHAPTER VIII

CONTROL, GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION Article 18

(1) Control, guidance and supervision of the provision of protection to victims of gender-based violence and violence against children shall be carried out by the Regent.

(2) The implementation of control, guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be assisted by the relevant Regional Work Unit.

Article 2

Letter a

What is meant by "non-discrimination" is protection for all victims of gender-based violence and children without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race, class, sex, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status and physical or mental condition.

Letter b

What is meant by "best interests of the victim" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

Letter c

What is meant by "gender justice" is fair treatment given to both women and men.

What is meant by "gender equality" is a condition and position that describes harmonious, congruent and balanced relations between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances in access, participation, control and benefits in the implementation of development and enjoying the results of development in family life as well as in society, nationhood and statehood.

Letter d

What is meant by "victim protection" is providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

Letter e

What is meant by "survival of the child" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to identity.

What is meant by "growth and development of the child" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to create and recreate.

Letter f

What is meant by "respect for the views of the child" is respect for the rights of children to participate and express their opinions in decision-making which can be taken into consideration especially if it concerns matters that affect their life.

Letter g

What is meant by "openness" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is transparent among the integrated service providers.

Letter h

What is meant by "integration" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is carried out by building coordination among service providers, including medical services, legal assistants, psychologists, clergy, social workers, police.

Letter i

What is meant by "empowerment" is that every effort given must be able to strengthen victims, both physically, psychologically, socially and economically.

Letter j

What is meant by "victim confidentiality" is every action taken to ensure victims are in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the life and psychology of victims.

Article 9

Prevention efforts as referred to in Article 7 paragraph (3) point a include:

a. conducting communication, information, and education on gender-based violence and violence against children; and
b. socialization of laws and regulations related to gender-based violence and violence against children.

Article 12

Coordination and cooperation as referred to in Article 7 paragraph (3) point d include:

a. conducting coordination and cooperation in handling violence cases with district/city integrated services;
b. conducting coordination and cooperation with institutions providing services for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children; and
c. conducting coordination and consultation with the Regional Government.

Article 19

All activities related to the provision of protection to victims of gender-based violence and violence against children shall be charged to the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget and other sources that are legal and non-binding.

Article 6

In providing protection to victims of gender-based violence and child victims of violence, the Regional Government is assisted by Integrated Services.

Article 5

Paragraph (1) Letter a Sufficiently clear. Letter b Sufficiently clear. Letter c Sufficiently clear Letter d Sufficiently clear Letter e What is meant by "cooperation" is a systematic and integrated way among organizers of protection and handling of victims of violence in providing services for victims of gender-based violence and children.

Letter f Sufficiently clear. Paragraph (2) Sufficiently clear. Paragraph (3) Sufficiently clear.

Article 14

Monitoring and reporting as referred to in Article 7 paragraph (3) point f shall be conducted on all aspects of integrated service activities in the form of implementing supervision, documentation and evaluation of cases of gender-based violence and violence against children.

Article 11

Legal protection as referred to in Article 7 paragraph (3) point c includes:

a. providing accompaniment during the legal process at every stage of examination; and
b. providing special legal protection for child victims of violence can be carried out through the appointment of guardianship in accordance with the prevailing regulations.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Central Government hereinafter referred to as Government is the President of the Republic of Indonesia who holds the governmental power of the State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
2. Region is Kudus Regency.
3. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
4. Regent is the Regent of Kudus.
5. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter referred to as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Kudus Regency.
6. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit responsible for women's empowerment and child protection.
7. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
8. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society.
9. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
10. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
11. Protection implementation is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the responsible SKPD.
12. Violence is any form of unlawful act that can result in or cause harm to a person whether physical, sexual, psychological and economic in nature.
13. Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment carried out on the basis of gender and aimed at reducing, eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
14. Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment carried out against children, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.
15. Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, illness, or serious injury.
16. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
17. Psychological Violence or psychic violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person.
18. Economic Violence is any act that may include restricting a person's right to work properly inside or outside the home and also acts of neglecting family members in the form of not providing proper livelihood, care or maintenance.
19. Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who because of their gender experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses caused by state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
20. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment whether physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual, and other losses caused by state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
21. Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to become more empowered, whether physical, psychological, social, economic or sexual.

23. Integrated Services is a series of activities to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unified implementation, prevention efforts, health services, medicolegal services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
24. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes that can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.

26. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations, and/or community organizations.

Letter g

What is meant by "openness" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is transparent among the integrated service providers.

Letter h

What is meant by "integration" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is carried out by building coordination among service providers, including medical services, legal assistants, psychologists, clergy, social workers, police.

Letter i

What is meant by "empowerment" is that every effort given must be able to strengthen victims, both physically, psychologically, socially and economically.

Letter j

What is meant by "victim confidentiality" is every action taken to ensure victims are in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the life and psychology of victims.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS OF GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important role in the development of a nation. Women as mothers of the nation who will give birth to children and children as the next generation of the nation are the capital of national development that need to receive legal protection from acts of gender-based violence and against children.

Gender-based violence and violence against children are increasingly prevalent today. Several forms of violence against women and children occurring in society may include social harassment, rape, trafficking of women and children, pornography, sexual exploitation, neglect, domestic violence. Therefore, legal instruments are needed that can guarantee the implementation of protection for the rights of women and children both at the national and regional levels.

In order to realize protection of the rights of women and children from the threat of acts of violence as mentioned above, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important role in the development of a nation. Women as mothers of the nation who will give birth to children and children as the next generation of the nation are the capital of national development that need to receive legal protection from acts of gender-based violence and against children.

Gender-based violence and violence against children are increasingly prevalent today. Several forms of violence against women and children occurring in society may include social harassment, rape, trafficking of women and children, pornography, sexual exploitation, neglect, domestic violence. Therefore, legal instruments are needed that can guarantee the implementation of protection for the rights of women and children both at the national and regional levels.

In order to realize protection of the rights of women and children from the threat of acts of violence as mentioned above, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Central Government hereinafter referred to as Government is the President of the Republic of Indonesia who holds the governmental power of the State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
2. Region is Kudus Regency.
3. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
4. Regent is the Regent of Kudus.
5. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter referred to as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Kudus Regency.
6. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit responsible for women's empowerment and child protection.
7. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
8. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society.
9. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
10. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
11. Protection implementation is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the responsible SKPD.
12. Violence is any form of unlawful act that can result in or cause harm to a person whether physical, sexual, psychological and economic in nature.
13. Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment carried out on the basis of gender and aimed at reducing, eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
14. Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment carried out against children, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.
15. Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, illness, or serious injury.
16. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
17. Psychological Violence or psychic violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person.
18. Economic Violence is any act that may include restricting a person's right to work properly inside or outside the home and also acts of neglecting family members in the form of not providing proper livelihood, care or maintenance.
19. Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who because of their gender experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses caused by state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
20. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment whether physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual, and other losses caused by state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
21. Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to become more empowered, whether physical, psychological, social, economic or sexual.
22. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems they face.
23. Integrated Services is a series of activities to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unified implementation, prevention efforts, health services, medicolegal services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
24. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes that can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.
25. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with established operational standards.
26. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations, and/or community organizations.

What is meant by "non-discrimination" is protection for all victims of gender-based violence and children without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race, class, sex, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status and physical or mental condition.

Letter b

What is meant by "best interests of the victim" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

Letter c

What is meant by "gender justice" is fair treatment given to both women and men.

What is meant by "gender equality" is a condition and position that describes harmonious, congruent and balanced relations between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances in access, participation, control and benefits in the implementation of development and enjoying the results of development in family life as well as in society, nationhood and statehood.

Letter d

What is meant by "victim protection" is providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

Letter e

What is meant by "survival of the child" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to identity.

What is meant by "growth and development of the child" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to create and recreate.

Letter f

What is meant by "respect for the views of the child" is respect for the rights of children to participate and express their opinions in decision-making which can be taken into consideration especially if it concerns matters that affect their life.

Letter g

What is meant by "openness" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is transparent among the integrated service providers.

Letter h

What is meant by "integration" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is carried out by building coordination among service providers, including medical services, legal assistants, psychologists, clergy, social workers, police.

Letter i

What is meant by "empowerment" is that every effort given must be able to strengthen victims, both physically, psychologically, socially and economically.

Letter j

What is meant by "victim confidentiality" is every action taken to ensure victims are in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the life and psychology of victims.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Central Government hereinafter referred to as Government is the President of the Republic of Indonesia who holds the governmental power of the State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.

7. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
8. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society.
9. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
10. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
11. Protection implementation is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the responsible SKPD.
12. Violence is any form of unlawful act that can result in or cause harm to a person whether physical, sexual, psychological and economic in nature.
13. Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment carried out on the basis of gender and aimed at reducing, eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
14. Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment carried out against children, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.
15. Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, illness, or serious injury.
16. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
17. Psychological Violence or psychic violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person.
18. Economic Violence is any act that may include restricting a person's right to work properly inside or outside the home and also acts of neglecting family members in the form of not providing proper livelihood, care or maintenance.
19. Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who because of their gender experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses caused by state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
20. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment whether physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual, and other losses caused by state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
21. Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to become more empowered, whether physical, psychological, social, economic or sexual.
22. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems they face.
23. Integrated Services is a series of activities to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unified implementation, prevention efforts, health services, medicolegal services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
24. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes that can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.
25. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with established operational standards.
26. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations, and/or community organizations.

11. Protection implementation is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the responsible SKPD.
12. Violence is any form of unlawful act that can result in or cause harm to a person whether physical, sexual, psychological and economic in nature.
13. Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment carried out on the basis of gender and aimed at reducing, eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
14. Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment carried out against children, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.
15. Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, illness, or serious injury.
16. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
17. Psychological Violence or psychic violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person.
18. Economic Violence is any act that may include restricting a person's right to work properly inside or outside the home and also acts of neglecting family members in the form of not providing proper livelihood, care or maintenance.
19. Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who because of their gender experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses caused by state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
20. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment whether physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual, and other losses caused by state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
21. Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to become more empowered, whether physical, psychological, social, economic or sexual.
22. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems they face.
23. Integrated Services is a series of activities to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unified implementation, prevention efforts, health services, medicolegal services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
24. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes that can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.
25. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with established operational standards.
26. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations, and/or community organizations.

Article 2

Letter a

What is meant by "non-discrimination" is protection for all victims of gender-based violence and children without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race, class, sex, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status and physical or mental condition.

Letter b

What is meant by "best interests of the victim" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

Letter c

What is meant by "gender justice" is fair treatment given to both women and men.

What is meant by "gender equality" is a condition and position that describes harmonious, congruent and balanced relations between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances in access, participation, control and benefits in the implementation of development and enjoying the results of development in family life as well as in society, nationhood and statehood.

Letter d

What is meant by "victim protection" is providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

Letter e

What is meant by "survival of the child" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to identity.

What is meant by "growth and development of the child" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to create and recreate.

Letter f

What is meant by "respect for the views of the child" is respect for the rights of children to participate and express their opinions in decision-making which can be taken into consideration especially if it concerns matters that affect their life.

Letter g

What is meant by "openness" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is transparent among the integrated service providers.

Letter h

What is meant by "integration" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is carried out by building coordination among service providers, including medical services, legal assistants, psychologists, clergy, social workers, police.

Letter i

What is meant by "empowerment" is that every effort given must be able to strengthen victims, both physically, psychologically, socially and economically.

Letter j

What is meant by "victim confidentiality" is every action taken to ensure victims are in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the life and psychology of victims.

Article 9

Prevention efforts as referred to in Article 7 paragraph (3) point a include:

a. conducting communication, information, and education on gender-based violence and violence against children; and
b. socialization of laws and regulations related to gender-based violence and violence against children.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important role in the development of a nation. Women as mothers of the nation who will give birth to children and children as the next generation of the nation are the capital of national development that need to receive legal protection from acts of gender-based violence and against children.

Gender-based violence and violence against children are increasingly prevalent today. Several forms of violence against women and children occurring in society may include social harassment, rape, trafficking of women and children, pornography, sexual exploitation, neglect, domestic violence. Therefore, legal instruments are needed that can guarantee the implementation of protection for the rights of women and children both at the national and regional levels.

In order to realize protection of the rights of women and children from the threat of acts of violence as mentioned above, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children.

Therefore, legal instruments are needed that can guarantee the implementation of protection for the rights of women and children both at the national and regional levels.

In order to realize protection of the rights of women and children from the threat of acts of violence as mentioned above, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important role in the development of a nation. Women as mothers of the nation who will give birth to children and children as the next generation of the nation are the capital of national development that need to receive legal protection from acts of gender-based violence and against children.

Gender-based violence and violence against children are increasingly prevalent today. Several forms of violence against women and children occurring in society may include social harassment, rape, trafficking of women and children, pornography, sexual exploitation, neglect, domestic violence. Therefore, legal instruments are needed that can guarantee the implementation of protection for the rights of women and children both at the national and regional levels.

In order to realize protection of the rights of women and children from the threat of acts of violence as mentioned above, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS OF GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important role in the development of a nation. Women as mothers of the nation who will give birth to children and children as the next generation of the nation are the capital of national development that need to receive legal protection from acts of gender-based violence and against children.

Gender-based violence and violence against children are increasingly prevalent today. Several forms of violence against women and children occurring in society may include social harassment, rape, trafficking of women and children, pornography, sexual exploitation, neglect, domestic violence. Therefore, legal instruments are needed that can guarantee the implementation of protection for the rights of women and children both at the national and regional levels.

In order to realize protection of the rights of women and children from the threat of acts of violence as mentioned above, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 2

Letter b

Letter c

What is meant by "gender equality" is a condition and position that describes harmonious, congruent and balanced relations between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances in access, participation, control and benefits in the implementation of development and enjoying the results of development in family life as well as in society, nationhood and statehood.

Letter d

What is meant by "victim protection" is providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

Letter e

What is meant by "survival of the child" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to identity.

What is meant by "growth and development of the child" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to create and recreate.

Letter f

Letter g

Letter h

Letter i

Letter j

(1) Control, guidance and supervision of the provision of protection to victims of gender-based violence and violence against children shall be carried out by the Regent.

(2) The implementation of control, guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be assisted by the relevant Regional Work Unit.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Central Government hereinafter referred to as Government is the President of the Republic of Indonesia who holds the governmental power of the State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
2. Region is Kudus Regency.
3. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
4. Regent is the Regent of Kudus.
5. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter referred to as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Kudus Regency.
6. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit responsible for women's empowerment and child protection.
7. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
8. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society.
9. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
10. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
11. Protection implementation is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the responsible SKPD.
12. Violence is any form of unlawful act that can result in or cause harm to a person whether physical, sexual, psychological and economic in nature.
13. Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment carried out on the basis of gender and aimed at reducing, eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
14. Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment carried out against children, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.
15. Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, illness, or serious injury.
16. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
17. Psychological Violence or psychic violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person.
18. Economic Violence is any act that may include restricting a person's right to work properly inside or outside the home and also acts of neglecting family members in the form of not providing proper livelihood, care or maintenance.
19. Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who because of their gender experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses caused by state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
20. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment whether physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual, and other losses caused by state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
21. Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to become more empowered, whether physical, psychological, social, economic or sexual.
22. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems they face.
23. Integrated Services is a series of activities to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unified implementation, prevention efforts, health services, medicolegal services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
24. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes that can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.
25. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with established operational standards.
26. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations, and/or community organizations.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS OF GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important role in the development of a nation. Women as mothers of the nation who will give birth to children and children as the next generation of the nation are the capital of national development that need to receive legal protection from acts of gender-based violence and against children.

Gender-based violence and violence against children are increasingly prevalent today. Several forms of violence against women and children occurring in society may include social harassment, rape, trafficking of women and children, pornography, sexual exploitation, neglect, domestic violence. Therefore, legal instruments are needed that can guarantee the implementation of protection for the rights of women and children both at the national and regional levels.

In order to realize protection of the rights of women and children from the threat of acts of violence as mentioned above, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 17

(1) In providing protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government, Provincial Government, and District/City Government, and other institutions.

(2) Cooperation between the Regional Government and the Government and Provincial Government as referred to in paragraph (1) includes consultation, coordination and reporting.

(3) Cooperation between the Regional Government and the District/City as referred to in paragraph (1) includes coordination, advocacy, referral, repatriation, social reintegration, facilitation of the development of integrated service systems, monitoring, evaluation and reporting.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Central Government hereinafter referred to as Government is the President of the Republic of Indonesia who holds the governmental power of the State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
2. Region is Kudus Regency.
3. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
4. Regent is the Regent of Kudus.
5. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter referred to as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Kudus Regency.
6. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit responsible for women's empowerment and child protection.
7. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
8. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society.
9. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
10. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
11. Protection implementation is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the responsible SKPD.
12. Violence is any form of unlawful act that can result in or cause harm to a person whether physical, sexual, psychological and economic in nature.
13. Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment carried out on the basis of gender and aimed at reducing, eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
14. Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment carried out against children, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.
15. Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, illness, or serious injury.
16. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
17. Psychological Violence or psychic violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person.
18. Economic Violence is any act that may include restricting a person's right to work properly inside or outside the home and also acts of neglecting family members in the form of not providing proper livelihood, care or maintenance.
19. Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who because of their gender experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses caused by state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
20. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment whether physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual, and other losses caused by state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
21. Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to become more empowered, whether physical, psychological, social, economic or sexual.
22. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems they face.
23. Integrated Services is a series of activities to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unified implementation, prevention efforts, health services, medicolegal services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
24. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes that can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.
25. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with established operational standards.
26. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations, and/or community organizations.

Article 2

Letter a

What is meant by "non-discrimination" is protection for all victims of gender-based violence and children without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race, class, sex, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status and physical or mental condition.

Letter b

What is meant by "best interests of the victim" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

Letter c

What is meant by "gender justice" is fair treatment given to both women and men.

What is meant by "gender equality" is a condition and position that describes harmonious, congruent and balanced relations between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances in access, participation, control and benefits in the implementation of development and enjoying the results of development in family life as well as in society, nationhood and statehood.

Letter d

What is meant by "victim protection" is providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

Letter e

What is meant by "survival of the child" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to identity.

What is meant by "growth and development of the child" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to create and recreate.

Letter f

What is meant by "respect for the views of the child" is respect for the rights of children to participate and express their opinions in decision-making which can be taken into consideration especially if it concerns matters that affect their life.

Letter g

What is meant by "openness" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is transparent among the integrated service providers.

Letter h

What is meant by "integration" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is carried out by building coordination among service providers, including medical services, legal assistants, psychologists, clergy, social workers, police.

Letter i

What is meant by "empowerment" is that every effort given must be able to strengthen victims, both physically, psychologically, socially and economically.

Letter j

What is meant by "victim confidentiality" is every action taken to ensure victims are in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the life and psychology of victims.

Article 21

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, orders the promulgation of this Regional Regulation by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Kudus Regency.

Enacted in Kudus on 23 December 2013

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS OF GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important role in the development of a nation. Women as mothers of the nation who will give birth to children and children as the next generation of the nation are the capital of national development that need to receive legal protection from acts of gender-based violence and against children.

Gender-based violence and violence against children are increasingly prevalent today. Several forms of violence against women and children occurring in society may include social harassment, rape, trafficking of women and children, pornography, sexual exploitation, neglect, domestic violence. Therefore, legal instruments are needed that can guarantee the implementation of protection for the rights of women and children both at the national and regional levels.

In order to realize protection of the rights of women and children from the threat of acts of violence as mentioned above, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 19

All activities related to the provision of protection to victims of gender-based violence and violence against children shall be charged to the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget and other sources that are legal and non-binding.

Article 2

Letter a

What is meant by "non-discrimination" is protection for all victims of gender-based violence and children without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race, class, sex, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status and physical or mental condition.

Letter b

What is meant by "best interests of the victim" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

Letter c

What is meant by "gender justice" is fair treatment given to both women and men.

What is meant by "gender equality" is a condition and position that describes harmonious, congruent and balanced relations between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances in access, participation, control and benefits in the implementation of development and enjoying the results of development in family life as well as in society, nationhood and statehood.

Letter d

What is meant by "victim protection" is providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

Letter e

What is meant by "survival of the child" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to identity.

What is meant by "growth and development of the child" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to create and recreate.

Letter f

What is meant by "respect for the views of the child" is respect for the rights of children to participate and express their opinions in decision-making which can be taken into consideration especially if it concerns matters that affect their life.

Letter g

What is meant by "openness" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is transparent among the integrated service providers.

Letter h

What is meant by "integration" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is carried out by building coordination among service providers, including medical services, legal assistants, psychologists, clergy, social workers, police.

Letter i

What is meant by "empowerment" is that every effort given must be able to strengthen victims, both physically, psychologically, socially and economically.

Letter j

What is meant by "victim confidentiality" is every action taken to ensure victims are in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the life and psychology of victims.

(1) In providing protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government, Provincial Government, and District/City Government, and other institutions.

(2) Cooperation between the Regional Government and the Government and Provincial Government as referred to in paragraph (1) includes consultation, coordination and reporting.

(3) Cooperation between the Regional Government and the District/City as referred to in paragraph (1) includes coordination, advocacy, referral, repatriation, social reintegration, facilitation of the development of integrated service systems, monitoring, evaluation and reporting.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Central Government hereinafter referred to as Government is the President of the Republic of Indonesia who holds the governmental power of the State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
2. Region is Kudus Regency.
3. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
4. Regent is the Regent of Kudus.
5. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter referred to as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Kudus Regency.
6. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit responsible for women's empowerment and child protection.
7. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
8. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society.
9. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
10. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
11. Protection implementation is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the responsible SKPD.
12. Violence is any form of unlawful act that can result in or cause harm to a person whether physical, sexual, psychological and economic in nature.
13. Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment carried out on the basis of gender and aimed at reducing, eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
14. Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment carried out against children, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.
15. Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, illness, or serious injury.
16. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
17. Psychological Violence or psychic violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person.
18. Economic Violence is any act that may include restricting a person's right to work properly inside or outside the home and also acts of neglecting family members in the form of not providing proper livelihood, care or maintenance.
19. Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who because of their gender experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses caused by state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
20. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment whether physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual, and other losses caused by state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
21. Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to become more empowered, whether physical, psychological, social, economic or sexual.
22. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems they face.
23. Integrated Services is a series of activities to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unified implementation, prevention efforts, health services, medicolegal services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
24. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes that can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.
25. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with established operational standards.
26. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations, and/or community organizations.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS OF GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important role in the development of a nation. Women as mothers of the nation who will give birth to children and children as the next generation of the nation are the capital of national development that need to receive legal protection from acts of gender-based violence and against children.

Gender-based violence and violence against children are increasingly prevalent today. Several forms of violence against women and children occurring in society may include social harassment, rape, trafficking of women and children, pornography, sexual exploitation, neglect, domestic violence. Therefore, legal instruments are needed that can guarantee the implementation of protection for the rights of women and children both at the national and regional levels.

In order to realize protection of the rights of women and children from the threat of acts of violence as mentioned above, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 19

All activities related to the provision of protection to victims of gender-based violence and violence against children shall be charged to the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget and other sources that are legal and non-binding.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Central Government hereinafter referred to as Government is the President of the Republic of Indonesia who holds the governmental power of the State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
2. Region is Kudus Regency.
3. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
4. Regent is the Regent of Kudus.
5. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter referred to as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Kudus Regency.
6. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit responsible for women's empowerment and child protection.
7. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
8. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society.
9. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
10. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
11. Protection implementation is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the responsible SKPD.
12. Violence is any form of unlawful act that can result in or cause harm to a person whether physical, sexual, psychological and economic in nature.
13. Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment carried out on the basis of gender and aimed at reducing, eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
14. Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment carried out against children, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.
15. Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, illness, or serious injury.
16. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
17. Psychological Violence or psychic violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person.
18. Economic Violence is any act that may include restricting a person's right to work properly inside or outside the home and also acts of neglecting family members in the form of not providing proper livelihood, care or maintenance.
19. Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who because of their gender experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses caused by state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
20. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment whether physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual, and other losses caused by state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
21. Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to become more empowered, whether physical, psychological, social, economic or sexual.
22. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems they face.
23. Integrated Services is a series of activities to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unified implementation, prevention efforts, health services, medicolegal services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
24. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes that can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.
25. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with established operational standards.
26. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations, and/or community organizations.

Article 6

In providing protection to victims of gender-based violence and child victims of violence, the Regional Government is assisted by Integrated Services.

Article 17

(1) In providing protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government, Provincial Government, and District/City Government, and other institutions.

(2) Cooperation between the Regional Government and the Government and Provincial Government as referred to in paragraph (1) includes consultation, coordination and reporting.

(3) Cooperation between the Regional Government and the District/City as referred to in paragraph (1) includes coordination, advocacy, referral, repatriation, social reintegration, facilitation of the development of integrated service systems, monitoring, evaluation and reporting.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS OF GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important role in the development of a nation. Women as mothers of the nation who will give birth to children and children as the next generation of the nation are the capital of national development that need to receive legal protection from acts of gender-based violence and against children.

Gender-based violence and violence against children are increasingly prevalent today. Several forms of violence against women and children occurring in society may include social harassment, rape, trafficking of women and children, pornography, sexual exploitation, neglect, domestic violence. Therefore, legal instruments are needed that can guarantee the implementation of protection for the rights of women and children both at the national and regional levels.

In order to realize protection of the rights of women and children from the threat of acts of violence as mentioned above, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children.
